L110: Addition (effective with 1.0.25):
L111:     Immediately below Equation (【74†1.13.4】), a sentence was added giving the definition of the $n$-argument Wronskian. It is explained just above (【75†1.13.5】) that this equation is often referred to as Abel’s identity. Immediately below Equation (【75†1.13.5】), a sentence was added explaining how it generalizes for $n$th-order differential equations, with a reference to Ince (【31†1926】, §5.2).

L114: The Wronskian of ${w}_{1}(z)$ and ${w}_{2}(z)$ is defined by
L115: 
L116: 1.13.4  |  | $$𝒲\left\{{w}_{1}(z),{w}_{2}(z)\right\}=det\left[\begin{array}{cc}{w}_{1}(z)& {w}_{2}(z)\\ {w}_{1}^{\prime }(z)& {w}_{2}^{\prime }(z)\end{array}\right]={w}_{1}(z){w}_{2}^{\prime }(z)-{w}_{2}(z){w}_{1}^{\prime }(z).$$  |

If $f(z)=0$, then the Wronskian is constant.
